links.detail: The Central Bank of Kenya awarded the contract to print new-look currency (Sh18 billion) to De La Rue International, which operates the Ruaraka plant co-owned by the Kenyan government; De La Rue beat Giesecke & Devrient, Crane Currency and Oberthur Fiduciaire. links.source_title: Business Daily Africa: CBK defends De La Rue new currency contract

links.detail: Sveriges Riksbank signed an agreement with De La Rue (announced 19 September 2018) to print Swedish banknotes for just over three years, replacing Crane.
links.source_title: Central Banking: De La Rue beats European competition to Swedish banknote contract

links.detail: Crane printed Liberian dollar banknotes for the Central Bank of Liberia under two contracts totalling L$15 billion at a cost of US$15,331,689.20.

links.relation: bribery or misconduct with the bank
links.detail: Liberia's Presidential Investigation Team alleged Crane conspired with CBL officials to print L$18,151,000,000, beyond the contracted L$15 billion. Crane denied wrongdoing and kickbacks and said it had not been charged; the PIT report also named former CBL Governor Charles Sirleaf. This is an allegation, not a finding by a court.
links.source_title: FrontPage Africa: Crane Currency Refutes Wrong Doing in L$16 Billion Saga

links.detail: Goznak (Russian state printer) printed Libyan dinars for the parallel eastern Central Bank (Benghazi/Bayda), which is not internationally recognized; Reuters-cited Russian customs data showed 4.5 billion dinars shipped Feb-June 2019. links.source_title: Middle East Institute (Jonathan M. Winer): Seized Russian-printed dinars...

links.detail: The MEI article states that the regular Libyan dinar notes are printed by Britain's De La Rue.

links.source_title: The History of the Note Printing Works (Bank of Thailand)

links.detail: A speech by the BSP Governor, published by the BIS, describes the Security Plant Complex as the facility housing the Bangko Sentral's currency production operations since 1978.
links.source_title: BSP Governor Benjamin Diokno, speech (BIS central bankers' speeches)

links.detail: PWPW signed an agreement with Banco de Guatemala, the central bank of Guatemala, on 20 August 2018 to produce 5- and 10-quetzal banknotes on a substrate containing synthetic fibres, with production to start later in 2018; PWPW's president called it the biggest order in its co-operation with the Guatemalan central bank to date. No contract value is stated.
links.source_title: PWPW to manufacture notes for Guatemala (Polska Wytwórnia Papierów Wartościowych)

links.detail: In a report on the Bank of Ghana's upgraded cedi notes signed on 4 March 2019 and announced on 8 April 2019, retired Bank of Ghana Deputy Governor Emmanuel Asiedu-Mante states that the cedi is printed by De La Rue, a security printing firm based in the United Kingdom, and that the printer charges in British pounds. No contract value is given.
links.source_title: See the company that prints the Ghana Cedi notes (Daily Graphic / Graphic Online)

links.detail: Danmarks Nationalbank has signed an agreement with De La Rue to produce Denmark's new banknote series at De La Rue's facility outside London; the notes are due for launch in 2028 and the contract runs for a minimum of six years with an option to extend. No value is stated.
links.source_title: De La Rue Wins Contract to Print Denmark's New Series (Currency News)

links.entity: Institute for Manufacturing Banknotes and Coins - Topčider
links.detail: The National Bank of Serbia states that its Institute at Topčider makes 'banknotes and coins issued by the NBS', alongside products for foreign countries; the Institute was built from 1927 and began operating in December 1929 as the Institute for Manufacturing Banknotes of the Kingdom of Yugoslavia, with a mint added in 1937.
links.source_title: Institute for Manufacturing Banknotes and Coins (National Bank of Serbia)

links.entity: Banknote Factory of the National Bank of Kazakhstan
links.detail: The National Bank of Kazakhstan lists the Banknote Factory of the National Bank among its subsidiaries and states that its main activity is the production of banknotes, along with other security printing (passports, ID and payment cards); the factory has released three series of tenge banknotes and eight commemorative or jubilee banknotes.
links.source_title: Subsidiaries (National Bank of Kazakhstan)

links.detail: Landqart states that the National Bank of Kazakhstan's 20,000 tenge banknote, issued for the 30th anniversary of Independence, is printed on Landqart's Durasafe composite substrate, and that it is the second note the bank has issued on that substrate; Landqart describes a partnership with the Banknote Factory of the National Bank of Kazakhstan.
links.source_title: The National Bank of Kazakhstan announce their new 20000 Tenge banknote (Landqart)

links.detail: A Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) press release on the NT$200 banknote states that 'the new banknotes are printed by China Engraving & Printing Works'.
links.source_title: Press release on the NT$200 banknote (Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan))

links.entity: Fábrica de Billetes del Banco de México
links.entity_hq_city: Mexico City and El Salto, Jalisco
links.detail: Banco de México makes its own banknotes in all denominations at its two banknote factories, in Mexico City and in El Salto, Jalisco; the notes it first circulated in 1925 were made by the American Bank Note Company of New York, and banknote printing moved to Banco de México's own factory in Mexico in 1969.
links.source_title: ¿Quién hace los billetes mexicanos? (Expansión)

links.entity: Banco de la República (Imprenta de Billetes)
links.detail: Banco de la República states that it itself carries out the production, issuance, supply, exchange and destruction of Colombia's banknotes and coins; its site navigation places the Imprenta de Billetes (banknote printing works) under its Central de Efectivo, and locates its coin plant at Ibagué, Tolima. The page does not give the printing works' location.
links.source_title: Emisión de la moneda legal colombiana (Banco de la República)

links.detail: Bank Al-Maghrib states that its industrial unit Dar As-Sikkah prints Morocco's banknotes and mints its coins, and also makes the national passport and other security documents; it was founded in 1987 and inaugurated by King Hassan II on 5 March 1987, a second banknote production line was added in 1992, it has printed foreign banknotes since 1995, and equipment modernisation began in 2008.
links.source_title: Activities of Dar As-Sikkah (Bank Al-Maghrib)

links.entity: Korea Minting and Security Printing Corporation (KOMSCO)
links.detail: The Korea Times describes KOMSCO as the state-run mint and 'the country's sole manufacturer of banknotes and coins', and says it maintains a close partnership with the Bank of Korea.
links.source_title: State-run mint debuts art exhibition highlighting printing technology (The Korea Times)

links.detail: De La Rue states that the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank's EC$2 commemorative polymer banknote is designed on De La Rue's SAFEGUARD polymer substrate and joins the all-polymer ECCB series first introduced in 2019; ECCB Governor Timothy Antoine is quoted saying 'in De La Rue, we have a partner on whom we can rely.' The release does not say who printed the note.
links.source_title: De La Rue: Eastern Caribbean Central Bank Unveils Innovative $2 Polymer Banknote (De La Rue plc, via MarketScreener)

links.entity: Casa de Moneda (Sociedad del Estado, Argentina)
links.detail: Argentina's state mint, Casa de Moneda, printed 1,000- and 2,000-peso banknotes for the Banco Central de la República Argentina under three contracts dated November 2021, September 2022 and February 2023; the BCRA partially rescinded those contracts and Casa de Moneda stopped banknote production at 10pm on 28 October 2024, with the government announcing that 2,000-peso notes would no longer be printed.
links.source_title: Cambio de época: la Casa de Moneda de Argentina suspende la impresión de billetes (Bloomberg Línea)

links.entity: Fábrica Nacional de Moneda y Timbre
links.detail: The report states that Casa de Moneda had outsourced production of Argentina's 2,000-peso banknotes to Spain's Fábrica Nacional de Moneda y Timbre, and that the Banco Central de la República Argentina will receive a small portion of those notes; it also says 20,000-peso notes were imported from China without naming the manufacturer.
links.source_title: Cambio de época: la Casa de Moneda de Argentina suspende la impresión de billetes (Bloomberg Línea)

links.detail: Louisenthal states that OFAD (Oberthur Fiduciaire AD) has handled Bulgarian National Bank banknote production since 2014.
links.source_title: Award-winning 100-lev note for Bulgaria (Louisenthal)

links.detail: Louisenthal states that it supplied the paper-embedded security features - the thread, the foil and the watermark - for the Bulgarian National Bank's 100-lev banknote, which became legal tender on 28 December 2018 and won the High Security Printing EMEA award in Malta in March 2019. No specific paper product is named.
links.source_title: Award-winning 100-lev note for Bulgaria (Louisenthal)

links.detail: The National Banknote Printing Factory is reported to be a one-member limited liability company with 100% charter capital held by the state and to be responsible for printing banknotes, with its board chairman appointed by the Governor of the State Bank of Vietnam and its production plans assigned by the Governor; Nguyen Duc Cuong was appointed chairman for a five-year term, succeeding Le Thai Nam, who had led it since September 2019.
links.source_title: National Banknote Printing Factory has new chairman (The Investor)

links.entity: Banknote Printing House, Central Bank of Egypt
links.detail: The Central Bank of Egypt's own Banknote Printing House in the New Administrative Capital handles the full banknote production process from design to delivery at the Cash Centre, and its output covers Egypt's domestic needs with capacity that could also supply other countries in the region; a BCEAO delegation toured it on 10 March 2025. No capacity figures are given.
links.source_title: Egypt showcases world-class banknote printing facility to West African delegation (Amwal Al Ghad)

links.detail: The South African Reserve Bank says the South African Bank Note Company (RF) Proprietary Limited prints South Africa's banknotes and that it is a subsidiary of the SARB.
links.source_title: Banknotes and coins production (South African Reserve Bank)
links.name_as_stated: the South African Bank Note Company (RF) Proprietary Limited (SABN)

links.detail: The Swiss National Bank states that Orell Füssli Security Printing Ltd prints the ninth series of Swiss franc banknotes.
links.source_title: Banknote production (Swiss National Bank)

links.detail: The Swiss National Bank states that Landqart supplies the three-layer banknote substrate Durasafe used for Swiss franc notes.
links.source_title: Banknote production (Swiss National Bank)

links.entity: Banknote Printing and Minting Works of the National Bank of Ukraine
links.detail: A National Bank of Ukraine interview states that hryvnia banknotes are printed at the Banknote Printing and Minting Works of the National Bank of Ukraine, which is part of the NBU.
links.source_title: Vasyl Ishchenko: Ukrainian money has sophisticated security features and enjoys high durability (National Bank of Ukraine)

links.detail: The same National Bank of Ukraine item states that the paper for hryvnia banknotes is made at the Banknote Paper Mill in Malyn; the source does not state its ownership.
links.source_title: Vasyl Ishchenko: Ukrainian money has sophisticated security features and enjoys high durability (National Bank of Ukraine)

links.detail: The Business Standard reports that Bangladesh's taka notes are printed by The Security Printing Corporation Limited, known locally as Takshal, at a site in Gazipur covering about 66 acres, in operation since 1989.
links.source_title: Where and how is our taka printed? (The Business Standard)

links.detail: The Banco de España states that IMBISA (Imprenta de Billetes S.A.), 80% owned by the Banco de España, prints the euro banknotes allocated to Spain, roughly 12% of total euro banknote production.
links.source_title: IMBISA: The banknotes factory that guarantees cash in Spain and the Eurosystem (Banco de España, Portal del Cliente Bancario)

links.detail: A joint Banque de France press release names OeBS as the banknote printer owned by the Oesterreichische Nationalbank, one of three central-bank-owned printers strengthening cooperation on banknote production.
links.source_title: Banque de France, OeNB and Banco de Portugal strengthen cooperation on banknote production (Banque de France)

links.detail: The same Banque de France press release names Valora as the banknote printer owned by the Banco de Portugal.
links.source_title: Banque de France, OeNB and Banco de Portugal strengthen cooperation on banknote production (Banque de France)

links.detail: Wikipedia states that the Security Printing and Minting Organization, a subsidiary of the Central Bank of Iran since 1962, is responsible for the design, production and elimination of banknotes and coinage in Iran, and that banknotes were printed abroad until 1982.
links.as_of: subsidiary since 23 September 1962; printing in Iran since 1982
links.source_title: Security Printing and Minting Organization (Wikipedia)

links.detail: The Jakarta Post reports that Bank Indonesia assigned Peruri, described as the state banknote printing firm, to print the new banknotes, which were printed at Peruri's facility in Karawang, West Java.
links.source_title: Peruri denies private firm in Central Java printed banknotes (The Jakarta Post)

links.entity: De La Rue Lanka Currency and Security Print (Pvt) Ltd
links.detail: The Central Bank of Sri Lanka states in its currency FAQ that its currency notes are printed by De La Rue Lanka Currency & Security Print (Pvt) Ltd at Biyagama, Sri Lanka.
links.source_title: Frequently Asked Questions - Currency (Central Bank of Sri Lanka)
links.name_as_stated: De La Rue Lanka Currency & Security Print (Pvt) Ltd

links.detail: The Magyar Nemzeti Bank states that forint banknotes are printed by the Hungarian Banknote Printing Company, an enterprise wholly owned by the MNB.
links.source_title: Production of banknotes and coins (Magyar Nemzeti Bank)

links.detail: The Magyar Nemzeti Bank states that the special paper for forint banknotes is made by the Diósgyőr Papermill, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Hungarian Banknote Printing Company.
links.source_title: Production of banknotes and coins (Magyar Nemzeti Bank)

links.detail: Addis Fortune reports that the National Bank of Ethiopia awarded Francois-Charles Oberthur Fiduciaire of France a 19.6 million Br share of a 206 million Br banknote printing deal, covering the 50 Br note.
links.source_title: Two Overseas Firms Seal Deal to Print Banknotes (Addis Fortune)

links.detail: Addis Fortune reports that the National Bank of Ethiopia awarded De La Rue of the United Kingdom a 187 million Br share of a 206 million Br banknote printing deal, covering the 100 Br note.
links.source_title: Two Overseas Firms Seal Deal to Print Banknotes (Addis Fortune)

links.entity: World Bank Treasury Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership (RAMP)
links.detail: The World Bank Treasury's RAMP global network page lists the Bank of Guatemala as a RAMP member institution; RAMP's own description of the partnership covers advisory services, executive training and asset management for members, and the page does not say which of these Guatemala receives.
links.source_title: Global Network - Reserve Advisory & Management Partnership (World Bank Treasury)

links.entity: World Bank Treasury Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership (RAMP)
links.detail: The World Bank Treasury's RAMP global network page lists the Central Bank of Trinidad and Tobago as a RAMP member institution; the page does not state whether the relationship is advice, training or management of assets, only that RAMP offers all three to members.
links.source_title: Global Network - Reserve Advisory & Management Partnership (World Bank Treasury)
links.name_as_stated: Central Bank of Trinidad and Tobago

links.entity: World Bank Treasury Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership (RAMP)
links.detail: The World Bank Treasury's RAMP global network page lists the National Bank of Cambodia as a RAMP member institution; the page does not state whether the relationship is advice, training or management of assets.
links.source_title: Global Network - Reserve Advisory & Management Partnership (World Bank Treasury)

links.entity: World Bank Treasury Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership (RAMP)
links.detail: The World Bank Treasury's RAMP global network page lists the Bulgarian National Bank as a RAMP member institution and as a co-host of a RAMP forum; the page does not state whether the relationship is advice, training or management of assets.
links.source_title: Global Network - Reserve Advisory & Management Partnership (World Bank Treasury)

links.entity: World Bank Treasury Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership (RAMP)
links.detail: The World Bank Group states that the Central Bank of Ecuador joined RAMP, giving it access to World Bank Group advisory services, executive training and asset management expertise; the release describes advice, training and expertise rather than a mandate to manage Ecuador's reserves.
links.source_title: World Bank Group RAMP welcomes Central Bank of Ecuador as new member (World Bank)

links.entity: World Bank Treasury Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership (RAMP)
links.detail: The World Bank states the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe joined RAMP through a multi-donor trust fund and signed a technical assistance agreement; the release describes technical assistance to strengthen the bank's public asset management capability, not management of its reserves.
links.source_title: World Bank RAMP announces new member Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe (World Bank)

links.entity: World Bank Treasury Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership (RAMP)
links.detail: The World Bank states the Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina signed a legal agreement joining RAMP, which provides members with advisory services, training and asset management services; the release does not say which of these the CBBH takes.
links.source_title: Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina joins World Bank RAMP to enhance reserve management (World Bank)
links.name_as_stated: Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina (CBBH)

links.entity: World Bank Treasury Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership (RAMP)
links.detail: The World Bank states the Central Bank of Armenia rejoined RAMP for advisory services and training resources, with RAMP providing onsite expertise to improve its reserve management operations and training for new staff; it was a member from 2006 to 2014. This is advice and training, not management of assets.
links.source_title: Central Bank of the Republic of Armenia rejoins World Bank Reserve Advisory & Management Partnership (World Bank)
links.name_as_stated: Central Bank of the Republic of Armenia (CBA)

links.entity: World Bank Treasury Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership (RAMP)
links.detail: The World Bank states the Central Bank of Paraguay joined RAMP in 2017 and that RAMP provided advisory services and executive training that helped the bank rebuild its own investment policy and diversify reserves away from bank deposits; the bank runs the portfolio itself, so this is advice and training rather than management of assets.
links.source_title: A partner in Paraguay: transforming reserve management at the Central Bank of Paraguay with World Bank RAMP (World Bank)

links.entity: World Bank Treasury Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership (RAMP)
links.detail: The Central Bank of the Republic of Kosovo states it became a RAMP member under an agreement with the World Bank Treasury, described as designed to increase the institution's capacity and expertise in asset management, risk management and financial reporting; this is advice, training and capacity building, not management of its reserves.
links.as_of: announced at the IMF-World Bank annual meetings, Marrakesh (2023)
links.source_title: Governor Ismaili after CBK's membership in the World Bank Treasury's RAMP program (Central Bank of the Republic of Kosovo)
links.name_as_stated: Central Bank of the Republic of Kosovo (CBK)

links.entity: World Bank Treasury Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership (RAMP)
links.detail: The World Bank states the Central Bank of Cabo Verde signed a technical assistance agreement delivering RAMP technical advisory services and became the 75th member of the RAMP network; the release describes advisory services, not management of assets.
links.source_title: World Bank RAMP trust fund to improve public asset management announces second beneficiary: Cabo Verde (World Bank)

links.entity: World Bank Treasury Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership (RAMP)
links.detail: The World Bank states the Central Bank of Liberia joined RAMP and signed a technical assistance agreement to build its public asset management capacity; the release describes technical assistance and training, and does not say RAMP manages CBL assets.
links.source_title: Central Bank of Liberia joins World Bank RAMP, global partnership of public asset managers (World Bank)

links.entity: World Bank Treasury Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership (RAMP)
links.detail: The Central Bank of Libya states it signed a cooperation agreement under the World Bank's RAMP framework at World Bank headquarters, aimed at better returns on its foreign currency reserves through international best practice in asset allocation, portfolio and risk management, plus human capital, accounting and legal development; the bank describes exchange of expertise and capacity building, not handing reserves to RAMP to manage.
links.source_title: Central Bank of Libya signs cooperation agreement under the RAMP program (Central Bank of Libya)
links.name_as_stated: Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership (RAMP) program

links.entity: World Bank Treasury Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership (RAMP)
links.detail: The Central Bank of Seychelles reports that RAMP runs an externally managed portfolio of its international reserves, first funded with US$100 million in 2019 and still held at end-2025, and that RAMP also delivered workshops and executive forums and sponsored staff qualifications during 2025; this is actual management of assets alongside advice and training.
links.source_title: International Reserves Management Report 2025 (Central Bank of Seychelles)
links.name_as_stated: World Bank's Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership (RAMP)

links.detail: The Central Bank of Seychelles reports that Crown Agents Investment Management runs an externally managed fixed income portfolio of its reserves, split 50-50 between US dollars and Chinese renminbi, with a mandate that began in 2014 at US$25.0 million and a further US$25.0 million added in April 2022; this is actual management of assets.
links.source_title: International Reserves Management Report 2025 (Central Bank of Seychelles)

links.detail: The Central Bank of Seychelles reports that UBS manages a money market fund holding part of its reserves, initially funded with US$10.0 million in 2017 and still held at end-2025, and that UBS also invited bank staff to its annual reserves management seminar; this is management of assets plus training.
links.source_title: International Reserves Management Report 2025 (Central Bank of Seychelles)

links.detail: Chile's Ministry of Finance states BNP Paribas Asset Management is the sole external manager of the US agency mortgage-backed securities portfolio of Chile's sovereign wealth funds, and that the Banco Central de Chile runs the selection of external managers, manages the sovereign fixed income share of the funds itself, and supervises external managers investing in instruments eligible for the international reserves; this is management of assets.
links.as_of: page current as of 2026 (notes Western Asset Management's exit in September 2024)
links.source_title: Quien administra los fondos actualmente? - Fondos Soberanos (Ministerio de Hacienda, Chile)

links.detail: Chile's Ministry of Finance states BlackRock Institutional Trust Company manages the high yield bond and corporate bond portfolios of Chile's sovereign wealth funds, for which the Banco Central de Chile runs the external manager selection process and supervises managers investing in instruments eligible for the international reserves; this is management of assets.
links.as_of: page current as of 2026 (notes Western Asset Management's exit in September 2024)
links.source_title: Quien administra los fondos actualmente? - Fondos Soberanos (Ministerio de Hacienda, Chile)

links.detail: Chile's Ministry of Finance states Nomura Asset Management manages part of the high yield bond portfolio of Chile's sovereign wealth funds, for which the Banco Central de Chile runs the external manager selection process and supervises managers investing in instruments eligible for the international reserves; this is management of assets.
links.as_of: page current as of 2026 (notes Western Asset Management's exit in September 2024)
links.source_title: Quien administra los fondos actualmente? - Fondos Soberanos (Ministerio de Hacienda, Chile)

links.detail: Chile's Ministry of Finance states UBS Asset Management Inc manages part of the corporate bond portfolio and part of the equity portfolio of Chile's sovereign wealth funds, for which the Banco Central de Chile runs the external manager selection process and supervises managers investing in instruments eligible for the international reserves; this is management of assets.
links.as_of: page current as of 2026 (notes Western Asset Management's exit in September 2024)
links.source_title: Quien administra los fondos actualmente? - Fondos Soberanos (Ministerio de Hacienda, Chile)

links.detail: Chile's Ministry of Finance states Mellon Investments Corporation manages part of the equity portfolio of Chile's sovereign wealth funds, for which the Banco Central de Chile runs the external manager selection process and supervises managers investing in instruments eligible for the international reserves; this is management of assets.
links.as_of: page current as of 2026 (notes Western Asset Management's exit in September 2024)
links.source_title: Quien administra los fondos actualmente? - Fondos Soberanos (Ministerio de Hacienda, Chile)

links.source_title: In Other News (Currency News, 31 March 2025)

links.entity: World Bank Reserves Advisory and Management Partnership (RAMP)
links.detail: The Central Bank of Somalia's own newsletter states that CBS became a member of the World Bank's Reserves Advisory and Management Program at the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings, and that through RAMP CBS gains access to technical support, advisory services and a network of global institutions; the source describes advice and technical support, not management of assets.
links.source_title: CBS Newsletter, Issue 004 (Central Bank of Somalia)
links.name_as_stated: World Bank's Reserves Advisory and Management Program (RAMP)

links.entity: World Bank Reserves Advisory and Management Partnership (RAMP)
links.detail: The National Bank of Georgia's own news item describes ongoing cooperation with the World Bank RAMP mission, covering the update of the foreign exchange reserves investment strategy and the enhancement of the gold management policy, with the Governor thanking the RAMP team for their technical assistance and continuous support; the source describes technical assistance and advice, not management of assets.
links.source_title: Natia Turnava Meets with World Bank RAMP Mission (National Bank of Georgia)

links.detail: The Bank of Papua New Guinea's annual report names Pictet among the external managers running part of its reserves portfolio, stating that Pictet recorded the weakest relative performance while DWS and BlackRock delivered the strongest results for the year; this is management of assets against the FTSE Russell Government Bond Index 1-3 Years USD Hedged benchmark.
links.source_title: Annual Report 2024 (Bank of Papua New Guinea)

links.source_title: Annual Report 2024 (Bank of Papua New Guinea)

links.detail: Central Banking's award profile states that the Central Bank of Eswatini moved its SDR-based portfolio to Crown Agents Investment Management in October 2023 after trying internal management, and that CAIM manages that portfolio while also training bank staff through regular calls, visits at least twice a year and an annual workshop; this is management of assets plus training.
links.as_of: portfolio moved to CAIM in October 2023; profile published 2026
links.source_title: Asset manager: Crown Agents Investment Management (Central Banking)

links.detail: Central Banking's award profile states that Crown Agents Investment Management manages about 95 percent of the Central Bank of the Solomon Islands' SDR allocation and has offered the bank online training on investment reporting and portfolio performance; this is management of assets plus training.
links.source_title: Asset manager: Crown Agents Investment Management (Central Banking)

links.detail: Central Banking's award profile states that Crown Agents Investment Management manages the Bank of Jamaica's SDR investments, which began at 250 million US dollars and have since doubled, and that the Bank of Jamaica gave CAIM discretion over how to invest them; this is management of assets.
links.source_title: Asset manager: Crown Agents Investment Management (Central Banking)

links.detail: Central Banking's award profile states that Amundi won a mandate from the Central Bank of Colombia (Banrep) in 2023 as one of eight outside managers, running an active fixed income programme for 1.7 billion US dollars of assets covering Treasuries, mortgage-backed securities and G10 currencies, and that the central bank was impressed by Amundi's knowledge-transfer proposal when screening managers; this is management of assets.
links.source_title: Asset manager: Amundi (Central Banking)

links.detail: Central Banking's award profile states that State Street Global Advisors holds an equity mandate for the Czech National Bank that was increased to 7.5 billion US dollars, with the CNB's executive director of risk management saying the bank has retained the equity mandate since 2007, and that SSGA also offers the CNB perspectives when it considers alternatives to its current reserve strategies; this is management of assets plus advice.
links.as_of: mandate held since 2007; profile published 21 January 2019
links.source_title: Asset manager of the year: State Street Global Advisors (Central Banking)

links.detail: Central Banking's award profile states that BlackRock is an outside manager for the equities and corporate parts of the Bank of Israel's portfolio, that it helped build the bank's strategic asset allocation methodology and still runs an independent annual allocation review the bank considers in its decisions, and that the Bank of Israel is a long-term client; this is management of assets plus advice.
links.as_of: activity described for 2017; profile published 29 January 2018
links.source_title: Asset manager of the year: BlackRock (Central Banking)

links.detail: Central Banking's award profile states that the Bank of Lithuania uses BlackRock's ETF services and that its staff have attended BlackRock's training sessions for central banks, which the bank's head of asset allocation called very useful; the source describes use of products and training, not a management mandate.
links.as_of: activity described for 2017; profile published 29 January 2018
links.source_title: Asset manager of the year: BlackRock (Central Banking)

links.detail: Central Banking's global custodian award profile states that the Bank of Botswana's deputy governor praised Northern Trust's service on performance measurement and attribution and on building the central bank's capacity, and that Northern Trust runs training for bank staff on benchmark construction and fixed-income investment; the source describes reporting services, capacity building and training, not management of assets.
links.source_title: Global custodian of the year: Northern Trust (Central Banking)

links.detail: Dabanga reported in February 2019 that Sudan's new 200-pound banknote went into production at the Sudanese Company for Currency Printing, a domestic press the prime minister visited that week; the report does not state the company's ownership.

links.source_title: Subordinate organizations (Central Bank of the Republic of Uzbekistan)

links.detail: Banco Central de Bolivia award resolution PRES-GAL No 19/2023, issued in La Paz on 27 July 2023, awarded its international banknote tender LPI 001-2023 to Oberthur Fiduciaire SAS for USD 25,945,787.00, covering 321.5 million notes of 10, 20, 50, 100 and 200 bolivianos.
links.source_title: Resolucion LPI 001-2023 adjudicacion (Banco Central de Bolivia)

links.detail: La Prensa reported that the Banco Central de Honduras awarded private tender 11/2023 to Crane Currency Malta Limited to print the 200-lempira note, by resolution 127-3/2024 of 14 March 2024, for USD 1,284,000 at 6.42 US cents per note.

links.detail: LexLatin reported on 27 March 2024 that Orell Fussli was partially awarded a tender "para la impresion y suministro de billetes del Banco Central de Nicaragua"; no value or quantity is given.

links.detail: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's page on Hong Kong notes states: "Banknotes issued by the note-issuing banks are printed in Hong Kong by Hong Kong Note Printing Limited (HKNPL)." links.source_title: Hong Kong Currency - Notes (Hong Kong Monetary Authority)

links.detail: An interview with the Bank of Mauritius published on the Bank's own website (a Currency News special issue for the Banknote 2014 conference) states that the Rs25 and Rs50 notes were supplied by Oberthur. links.source_title: Putting the 'Swing' into the New Mauritius Notes (Bank of Mauritius communique)

links.detail: An interview with the Bank of Mauritius published on the Bank's own website (a Currency News special issue for the Banknote 2014 conference) refers to "the Rs500 note supplied by De La Rue". links.source_title: Putting the 'Swing' into the New Mauritius Notes (Bank of Mauritius communique)

links.detail: PWPW's own news page states that it signed a contract with the Central Bank of Paraguay for "the production and delivery of 28 million banknotes of two denominations: 10 000 and 20 000 guarani". No contract value is given on either page.

links.detail: PWPW's own news page on its 2018 export results states that PWPW produced "55 million banknotes for the Dominican Republic", and lists "banknote contracts for Honduras, Paraguay and the Dominican Republic" among its successes. The page names no Dominican counterparty, gives no contract value, and states that "Most of PWPW contracts are secret."
links.source_title: The value of PWPW exports doubled in 2018 (PWPW)

links.detail: A Detik Finance report of 13 December 2022 states that Peruri has secured an order to print banknotes for Peru, calling Peru "pasar paling baru yang berhasil ditembus Peruri" (the newest market Peruri has successfully entered); it names no Peruvian counterparty and gives no contract value. An earlier Detik report of 8 January 2020 said Peruri had won the tender to print the 10, 20 and 50 nuevo sol denominations, with the contract then still to be signed.
links.source_title: Top! RI Cetak Duit buat Peru hingga Nepal, Kini Incar Argentina (Detik Finance)

links.detail: A De La Rue press release headed "The Bank of Albania launches new polymer banknote series, originated and printed by De La Rue" states that the series was "originated and produced by De La Rue", covering the 200, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000 and 10000 leke denominations, with the 200 and 5000 leke entering circulation "from 30 September" and the rest over the following three years. No year and no contract value are given on the page.
links.source_title: The Bank of Albania launches new polymer banknote series, originated and printed by De La Rue (press release)

links.detail: On a G+D page carrying an interview with the Central Bank of Armenia about its third banknote series, the Bank's representative answers the question "How did you select the banknote printer?" by saying "Giesecke+Devrient won as a result of a comprehensive evaluation of all offers." The page does not state in so many words that G+D printed the notes, and gives no contract value. Its dating is inconsistent: it is labelled "Published in Currency News June 2019" while the interview refers to the series being introduced "at the start of this year" and the page's meta description says the start of 2021.
links.as_of: page labelled "Published in Currency News June 2019"
links.source_title: Armenia - optimising its new series through design, security and substrate (Giesecke+Devrient)

links.detail: The Czech National Bank's description of its commemorative banknote marking the establishment of the Czechoslovak currency (Karel Englis) states that the reverse bears, in tiny letters near the lower edge, the inscription "STATNI TISKARNA CENIN, STATNI PODNIK, PRAHA". The page states no printing date; the note's year of issue is 2022 and it entered circulation on 30 March 2022. The page does not say who prints the Czech National Bank's circulating banknotes.
links.source_title: Commemorative banknote featuring a motif on the establishment of the Czechoslovak currency (Czech National Bank)
links.name_as_stated: STATNI TISKARNA CENIN, STATNI PODNIK, PRAHA

links.detail: Central Banking's award profile states that the Czech National Bank and BNP Paribas Asset Management agreed a new $500 million mortgage-backed securities mandate in November 2019; the profile describes a managed mandate, not advice or custody.
links.source_title: Asset manager: BNP Paribas Asset Management (Central Banking Awards 2021)

links.detail: Central Banking's award profile states that BNP Paribas Asset Management manages a fixed income mandate in US dollars for the Central Bank of Aruba, and quotes the bank's president Jeanette Semeleer saying that when the bank needed advice it could count on the firm; the profile describes management of a mandate plus advice.
links.source_title: Asset manager: BNP Paribas Asset Management (Central Banking Awards 2021)

links.detail: Central Banking's award profile states that the Central Bank of Hungary (MNB) awarded BNP Paribas Asset Management another mortgage mandate, for US agency mortgage-backed securities, in 2018, and quotes the MNB's Robert Rekasi saying the knowledge transfer the firm provides is crucial; the profile describes a managed mandate plus training.
links.source_title: Innovation in reserve management: BNP Paribas Asset Management (Central Banking Awards 2019)

links.detail: Financial Afrik reports that the governor of the Banque Centrale de Mauritanie, Sid'Ahmed Ould Raiss, and the World Bank's vice-president and treasurer Madelyn Antoncic signed a cooperation agreement on foreign exchange reserve management on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank spring meetings, and that the World Bank treasury department will provide technical assistance to the BCM covering training of reserve staff, organisation of the relevant structures and the eventual setting up of a trading room; the source describes technical assistance and training, not management of assets.
links.source_title: Mauritanie/Banque mondiale: convention pour la gestion des reserves en devises (Financial Afrik)
links.name_as_stated: le departement de la tresorerie de la Banque mondiale

links.detail: Semanario Universidad reports that the Banco Central de Costa Rica hired BlackRock as a co-administrator of its international reserves in 2017 and that BlackRock holds 5.5 percent of the reserves, about $352 million, with the BCCR telling the paper that hiring external portfolio managers is a usual practice in central banking; this is management of assets.
links.source_title: BlackRock: el golpeado gigante que administra reservas en dolares del Banco Central (Semanario Universidad)

links.detail: BanknoteNews states that, according to a ToloNews article of 6 January 2020, Da Afghanistan Bank awarded the Polish Security Printing Works (PWPW) a contract for new notes in 10, 20, 50 and 100 afghani denominations, and that on 1 February 2021 the Polish embassy in New Delhi announced that PWPW had delivered to Afghanistan 380 million newly printed banknotes. No contract value and no statement of an ongoing arrangement is given.
links.source_title: Afghanistan new 50-afghani note (B374a) confirmed

links.source_title: Quels sont les pays arabes qui impriment leur propre monnaie ?

links.detail: El Mostrador reports that Venezuela turned to the Russian state-owned money-printing company Goznak to print its banknotes, under a contract between Goznak and the Banco Central de Venezuela signed in November (on the article's account, November 2019). links.source_title: China Banknote Printing and Minting Corporation

links.detail: The Central Bank of Iceland's own announcement of the new 10,000 krona banknote states: 'The new notes were printed by De La Rue Plc. in the UK.' The statement covers that denomination only; the announcement says nothing about who prints Iceland's other notes.
links.source_title: New 10,000 kr. banknote in circulation

links.detail: A Reserve Bank of Fiji press release states that the bank 'signed an agreement for the printing of a series of new design Fiji banknotes with De La Rue International Limited' of the United Kingdom, and that a $100 note would be introduced for the first time. links.detail: A joint De La Rue / Bank of Botswana announcement, headlined 'Bank of Botswana announce introduction of a new polymer banknote, designed and printed by De La Rue', states that the new 10 pula polymer note was designed and printed by De La Rue; the note entered circulation on 1 February 2018. links.source_title: De La Rue: Bank of Botswana announce introduction of a new polymer banknote, designed and printed by De La Rue

links.source_title: Richard Byles: Launch of Jamaica's new series of banknotes (BIS Central Bankers' Speeches)

notes: All links come from pages or PDFs opened on 2026-10-24. Firm headquarters (entity_hq_city/iso3, firm_hq_iso3) are filled only where an opened source states the location; elsewhere they are null, even for well-known firms. The G30 Washington address comes from the G30 site footer; BIS and FSB are given as Basel.

entity_type 'state body' is used for public audit offices (ANAO, Auditor-General of Singapore, HK Director of Audit, Swedish NAO, BPK Indonesia, Thai SAO, Auditor General of Malaysia, the BoJ's Cabinet-appointed Auditors). This value is not in the requested enum; change it if your schema is strict.

G30: 29 current members plus 27 emeritus members, 56 records in all (Rajan and Tharman are current members who also hold leadership posts; Frenkel, Trichet and Ortiz are emeritus members who also hold leadership posts). Membership is from group30.org/members; posts are from each member's G30 bio page. The listing page says Maria Ramos is 'Chair, Standard Chartered Bank', but her bio says Senior Independent Director since 2022; both are recorded. Gail Kelly's UBS board seat appears on the listing page only. De la Dehesa's and Turner's corporate roles come from bios that may be out of date.
The G30 page names Mark Carney as Chair from 2023 to January 2025. The current Chair is Raghuram Rajan and the Chair of the Board of Trustees is Tharman Shanmugaratnam.

BIS Board: the BIS page gives each member's name and city only, so the home central bank (entity_hq_iso3) is inferred from the city. Kevin M Warsh is listed for Washington and Emmanuel Moulin for Paris, as of the page fetched 2026-10-24. Fabio Panetta has chaired the Board since 3 June 2026. Pablo Hernández de Cos has been General Manager since 1 July 2025.

FSB: these links are at institution level, from the FSB members page last updated 1 October 2026. Russia is a member, but its central bank representative is 'TBC' and the page says Russian authorities have agreed not to participate in FSB meetings at present. For ministries and regulators, cb_iso3 holds the country code.

Auditors: 27 central banks or monetary authorities (including the ECB) plus the BIS are covered (36 auditor links). Not found in an opened source: Bank of Italy, Bank of Korea, Banco de México, Saudi Central Bank, Bank of Russia, PBOC, Central Bank of Ireland, National Bank of Belgium, Bank of Israel, RBNZ, NBP, BSP, CBN and Banco Central de Chile (blocked by bot protection). The Czech National Bank's auditor report is an image in its PDF, so no firm could be read. For DNB (EY, FY2026-2032) and Bank of Finland (PwC, FY2026-2031), the record is the approved or recommended future auditor, not the signer of the 2025 accounts. The ECB auditor comes from the Council Decision (Forvis Mazars, FY2025-2029), not the signed report.

Printers: most client links come from contract notices, central bank press releases and trade press (Central Banking, Business Daily Africa, Curaçao Chronicle). The Crane client list for Mexico, Guyana and Aruba is a statement inside the CBCS announcement. G+D's Myanmar customer was the state Security Print Works, not the central bank. No documented bribery case was found for Oberthur Fiduciaire or Giesecke+Devrient. A World Bank settlement with 'Oberthur Technologies' (2017) came up in search, but it concerns a different company (cards and IDs) and was left out.

De La Rue SFO case: opened July 2019 and closed June 2020 (City A.M., 16 June 2020). The 2010 falsified paper certificates and the RBI supply suspension come from Central Banking (2010) and Eye Radio (2020). The 2010 Central Banking text did not name the RBI.
Securency/NPA: the RBA chronology lists the guilty pleas and pecuniary penalties under October and November 2011. Check the dates against court records if you need precision.

The OeBS bribery item is a prosecution allegation reported by GIR (21 Feb 2014). The outcome was not verified. Central Banking's headline that the OeNB vice-governor faced bribery charges was seen only in search results and was not opened, so it is not included.
Liberia/Crane and Nigeria/Emefiele items are allegations or charges, not convictions.

Asset managers: SNB says 99% of its foreign currency investments are managed internally and uses external managers for benchmarking and new asset classes, but publishes no names. RBI's 2025-26 accounts show fees to 'External Asset Managers, Custodians, Brokers' of Rs 176.72 crore, with no names. HKMA says external managers run about 29% of Exchange Fund assets (all listed equities), with no names. No links were made for these three. The Saudi Central Bank's external managers were not found.

NBIM: all 103 external managers listed as at 31 Dec 2025 are included unfiltered. A historical list (1998-2025) is published as an xlsx at https://www.nbim.no/contentassets/6a6080231c704160bf95faf6b34ab940/external-managers-1998-2025.xlsx (not downloaded).
Kosovo is coded XKX (not an ISO-assigned code). The Curaçao and Sint Maarten central bank is coded CUW.
